NextItNet stacks causal dilated convolutions with residual connections, expanding accessible history without pooling; theoretical reach does not establish which lags actually influence predictions. [Original NextItNet paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163). Effective-receptive-field research shows that influence can occupy only part of theoretical coverage, although its CNN findings require verification in sequential recommendation. [Luo et al.](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2016/hash/c8067ad1937f728f51288b3eb986afaa-Abstract.html). Searches found no directly matching 2024–2026 NextItNet activation-patching study. Relevant methodological work warns that corruption choice, output metric and jointly patched layer windows can substantially change localization conclusions. [Zhang and Nanda, revised 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042).

Practical adaptation: cache clean activations, replace recent or older history items while preserving length and padding, then restore individual block outputs at selected temporal positions. Measure both clean-to-corrupted restoration and corrupted-to-clean disruption; these provide different, context-dependent evidence about sufficiency and necessity. Prefer continuous candidate-score margins alongside rank and HR@10; inspect raw effects when normalized recovery has a small denominator. [Heimersheim and Nanda, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255). Proposed NextItNet controls: identical-input patches should leave scores unchanged; restoring all changed activations at a complete computation boundary should recover clean scores; positions outside the downstream causal receptive field should have no effect. Keep candidates fixed, disable dropout, preserve the final-nonpadding readout, repeat across plausible replacement histories, and distinguish residual-branch patches from whole-block patches that also overwrite skip-path information. Report block-by-lag effects as computational influence under specified interventions; they do not establish user intent or training-data causality.
